caption: : Avg. performance across 11 datasets (y-axis) consistently improves as the number of training examples increases (x-axis). Max is 29k examples, the full size of our dataset.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of training examples and the average performance across 11 datasets, as reported in the paper “Context-Informed Grounding Supervision.” The x-axis, labeled “# of training dataset (k),” represents the number of training examples in thousands, ranging from 5k to 30k, with major tick marks at 5k intervals (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). The y-axis, labeled “Average Performance,” is scaled linearly from 47 to 57, with major gridlines and tick labels every 1 unit. A single black solid line with circular markers connects five data points: at 5k examples, performance is approximately 47.5; at 10k, it rises to 50.3; at 20k, it reaches 52.7; and at 30k, it peaks at approximately 56.2. The trend is monotonically increasing, indicating consistent performance gains as more training data is added, with the maximum tested value corresponding to the full dataset size of 29k examples (plotted at 30k for visual alignment).
